title: Unveiling And Addressing Dimensional Collapse In Vector Quantization Models Via Codebook Regularization
claim: Discrete quantization collapses the representation spectrum into few dimensions, hurting fidelity; restoring the low-variance components recovers rank and quality.
layout: 2 panels: bar chart left, three image-plus-spectrum columns right
description: Panel (a) is a grouped bar chart comparing Standard VQ (red) with continuous AE (blue) on three metrics: effective rank (12.1 vs 37.2), D90 (10.2 vs 11.3) and D99 (11.9 vs 35.4). The numbers are printed above the bars, and the large gap in effective rank and D99 draws the eye first. Panel (b) has three columns: Continuous AE, Standard VQ and Ours. Each column has a reconstructed photo of pens, markers and glasses on a woven mat. Below each photo is a singular-value spectrum curve in blue, red or green, with dashed D90 and D99 markers. An inset box gives effective rank and rFID. Standard VQ is annotated with a 'Spectral Truncation' arrow where the red curve drops to zero early. Ours has a longer tail, an effective rank of 19.6 and a lower rFID of 1.50.
caption: (a) Comparison of effective dimensionality between Standard VQ and its continuous AE counterpart. (b) Spectral Truncation and Visual Fidelity: We compare reconstruction performance from a continuous Autoencoder (AE), a standard VQ-GAN, and our enhanced VQ with codebook regularization. Below each image are the SVD spectrum of its codebook/latent feature, along with its effective rank and rFID.
abstract: While recent advancements in Vector Quantization (VQ) models have successfully achieved complete codebook utilization, a critical bottleneck remains largely unexplored: the effective dimensionality of the codebook embedding space. We observe that discrete codebook representations tend to degenerate into low-dimensional subspaces, characterized by significantly lower effective rank than continuous representations during quantization. Through comprehensive spectral analysis, we identify that this dimensional collapse stems from the suppression of low-variance components inherent to the vector quantization process, thereby severely limiting the expressive capacity of VQ models. To mitigate this fundamental issue, we propose a simple yet effective codebook regularization strategy designed to restore low-variance components, effectively bridging the spectral gap between discrete codebook spaces and continuous representations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this regularization objective is compatible with diverse VQ training paradigms, yielding significant improvements in reconstruction fidelity and downstream performance in autoregressive image generative models.
